normative_concern.label: Access to justice
normative_concern.definition: Whether AI widens or narrows access to legal help, courts, and legal information.

normative_concern.label: Accountability and liability
normative_concern.definition: Who answers, and who is legally liable, for AI-produced legal work or decisions.

normative_concern.label: Accuracy and reliability
normative_concern.definition: Correctness, stability, hallucination, and dependability of AI outputs in legal use.

normative_concern.label: Autonomy and human oversight
normative_concern.definition: The degree of human control, review, and decision authority over AI in legal tasks.

normative_concern.label: Cost, efficiency and labour
normative_concern.definition: Cost savings, efficiency gains, and effects on legal labour and the legal profession.

normative_concern.label: Due process and fair trial
normative_concern.definition: Procedural rights, the right to be heard, and fair-trial guarantees when AI is used in proceedings.

normative_concern.label: Environmental cost
normative_concern.definition: Energy and environmental footprint of legal AI systems.

normative_concern.label: Explainability and transparency
normative_concern.definition: Whether AI outputs and processes can be explained, inspected, or understood.

normative_concern.label: Fairness and non-discrimination
normative_concern.definition: Bias, disparate impact, and equal treatment in AI-supported legal processes.

normative_concern.label: Privacy and data protection
normative_concern.definition: Personal data, confidentiality, and data-protection law in legal AI.

normative_concern.label: Professional responsibility
normative_concern.definition: Duties of lawyers, judges, and legal professionals when using AI (competence, verification, candour).

normative_concern.label: Rule of law and legitimacy
normative_concern.definition: Legitimacy, authority, and rule-of-law implications of AI in legal interpretation and adjudication.

normative_concern.label: Security and misuse
normative_concern.definition: Adversarial use, manipulation, security risks, and misuse of AI in legal settings.

legal_task.label: Access-to-justice tools
legal_task.definition: Tools that help laypeople or under-resourced parties navigate legal processes or documents.

legal_task.label: Adjudicative decision support
legal_task.definition: Supporting judges, tribunals, or adjudicators in deciding cases.

legal_task.label: Argument mining
legal_task.definition: Identifying and structuring argumentative units and rhetorical roles in legal text.

legal_task.label: Compliance and monitoring
legal_task.definition: Checking conduct, systems, or documents against legal or regulatory requirements.

legal_task.label: Drafting and generation
legal_task.definition: Generating legal text such as contracts, briefs, opinions, or answers.

legal_task.label: E-discovery
legal_task.definition: Identifying responsive or relevant documents in litigation document review.

legal_task.label: Entity and citation extraction
legal_task.definition: Extracting named entities, citations, and structured elements from legal text.

legal_task.label: Information retrieval
legal_task.definition: Finding relevant legal documents or passages (cases, statutes, precedents) for a query.

legal_task.label: Legal education
legal_task.definition: Use of AI in teaching, training, or examining legal knowledge and skills.

legal_task.label: Outcome prediction
legal_task.definition: Predicting the outcome, verdict, or decision of a legal case or proceeding.

legal_task.label: Question answering
legal_task.definition: Answering legal questions posed in natural language, including entailment over statutory text.

legal_task.label: Review and due diligence
legal_task.definition: Reviewing documents (contracts, filings) for risks, clauses, or issues.

legal_task.label: Rule formalisation
legal_task.definition: Translating legal rules or statutes into formal, machine-executable representations.

legal_task.label: Summarisation
legal_task.definition: Producing condensed versions of legal documents such as judgments or contracts.

technique_class.label: Agentic systems
technique_class.definition: Autonomous or semi-autonomous AI agents that plan, act, negotiate, or transact on behalf of users.

technique_class.label: Case-based reasoning
technique_class.definition: Reasoning from precedent cases by factor or dimension comparison.

technique_class.label: Classical statistical machine learning
technique_class.definition: Feature-based learners such as SVMs, logistic regression, random forests, and n-gram models.

technique_class.label: Computational argumentation
technique_class.definition: Formal models of argument structure, attack, and defeat applied to legal reasoning.

technique_class.label: Large language models
technique_class.definition: Large pre-trained generative language models such as GPT-3, GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, and Llama used by prompting or fine-tuning.

technique_class.label: Neuro-symbolic hybrids
technique_class.definition: Combinations of neural models with symbolic representations, logics, or reasoning engines.

technique_class.label: Pre-LLM neural models
technique_class.definition: Neural models predating large language models: CNNs, RNNs, BiLSTMs, and encoder models such as BERT fine-tuned for a task.

technique_class.label: Retrieval-augmented or tool-using systems
technique_class.definition: Language models combined with retrieval, external knowledge sources, or tools at inference time.

technique_class.label: Symbolic and rule-based systems
technique_class.definition: Hand-coded rules, logic programming, expert systems, and formal logics for legal reasoning.
